title: S&P 500 to Add SharkNinja as $33.4B AES Buyout Nears
summary: SharkNinja (SN) will join the S&P 500 on Dec. 2, replacing AES as a consortium takes the utility private in a $33.4 billion deal.
body_markdown:
## S&P 500 Entry Rules for a MidCap 400 Promotion


[S&P Dow Jones Indices](https://press.spglobal.com/2025-07-01-S-P-Dow-Jones-Indices-Announces-Update-to-S-P-Composite-1500-Market-Cap-Guidelines) noted in its July 1, 2025 update that S&P 500 additions need an unadjusted company market capitalization of $22.7 billion or more, a range it reviews every quarter.[S&P Dow Jones Indices](https://press.spglobal.com/2026-06-04-S-P-Dow-Jones-Indices-Consultation-on-Treatment-of-MegaCap-Companies-Results) said in its June 4, 2026 consultation results, which kept the eligibility rules unchanged, that additions also need positive GAAP net income from continuing operations for the latest quarter and the latest four quarters combined.


The same results state that a company moving between S&P Composite 1500 indexes, as SharkNinja is from the MidCap 400, need not meet the profit or liquidity tests.


## SharkNinja Shares Rise 2.1% After Hours


SharkNinja shares rose 2.1% in after-hours trading following the announcement, as reported by[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sharkninja-set-for-sp-500-entry-in-wave-of-dealdriven-index-changes-5046611) , while Guardian Pharmacy shares gained 2.5% in extended trading. The same report noted that an index addition requires passive and[index-tracking funds](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/index-funds-what-are-they-and-how-to-trade/) to buy the shares. Exchange-traded funds that track the large-cap benchmark, such as[SPY, VOO and IVV](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/sp-500-etf-explained-how-voo-ivv-and-spy-differ/) , are among them.


## SharkNinja Q3 Net Sales Rose 21.2%


The consumer appliance maker joins the index after a quarter of faster growth. Net sales rose 21.2% to $1,976.4 million in the third quarter ended September 30, from $1,630.2 million a year earlier, according to[SharkNinja's earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001957132/000195713226000055/exhibit991pressreleaseofsh.htm) .


> "Q3 net sales grew 21.2%, marking our second consecutive quarter above 20% and our 14th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth," SharkNinja CEO Mark Barrocas said in the release.


Net income per diluted share rose 79.7% to $2.39, while adjusted net income per diluted share increased 56.0% to $2.34. GAAP results included $109.6 million of refund claims for tariffs paid under IEEPA in fiscal 2025, which the company excluded from its adjusted figures.


SharkNinja also raised its full-year 2026 outlook and now expects net sales to grow 18.0% to 19.0%, up from its prior range of 16.0% to 17.0%.


## Transocean and Tecnoglass Move on December 1


The same S&P Dow Jones Indices announcement includes two changes effective before the open on Tuesday, December 1. Transocean (RIG) will replace Valaris (VAL) in the S&P MidCap 400 as it acquires Valaris, and Tecnoglass Holdings (TGLS) will replace MarineMax (HZO) in the S&P SmallCap 600, as a Blackstone Infrastructure portfolio company and Safe Harbor acquire MarineMax. Both deals are expected to close soon pending final conditions, the index provider said.
